Intro

  • Adderall (Amphetamine) is a stimulant medication that is used in the treatment of ADHD, It works by increasing the amounts of dopamine, norepinephrine and serotonin in the brain through variety of mechanisms
  • Adderall is generally well tolerated by most patients, but it sometimes may lead to side effects that will be mentioned here
  • Every person will have a different experience with the side effects

1. Reduced appetite and weight loss

  • Higher levels of dopamine and norepinephrine will affect the hypothalamus leading to suppression of the hunger feeling
  • Reduced appetite lead to reduced caloric intake which ultimately lead to weight loss
  • In children, this may lead to slowing the growth velocity and ultimately it may lead to reduction in adult height by around 4 cm in children who consistently took the medication

2. Increased heart rate and blood pressure

  • Higher levels of norepinephrine and dopamine lead to activation of the sympathetic nervous system
  • This will lead to activation of adrenergic receptors in the heart and blood vessels leading to elevated heart rate and blood pressure

3. Insomnia

  • Higher levels of dopamine and norepinephrine stimulate the CNS leading to wakefulness and inability to sleep

4. Headache

  • No good theory for why this happens

5. Dry mouth

  • Alpha adrenoceptors in the gums blood vessels get activated which lead to vasoconstriction in these blood vessels leading to less blood reaching the gums and less saliva production and dry mouth

6. Anxiety

  • Increased CNS activity can induce the feeling of anxiety

7. Vertigo

  • Altered levels of neurotransmitters can affect the vestibular system leading to vertigo

8. GIT side effects

  • Nausea and vomiting
  • That is because Increased norepinephrine levels also affects the enteric nervous system leading to nausea and vomiting
  • Also Elevated norepinephrine levels may stimulate the chemoreceptor trigger zone in the brain leading to nausea and vomiting

9. Sexual side effects

  • Those include erectile dysfunction, frequent and prolonged erections
  • Norepinephrine can affect the alpha adrenergic receptors in the genital region, which can affect blood flow and nerve signaling leading to sexual side effects

10. Respiratory side effects

  • Amphetamine stimulates the medullary respiratory centers producing faster and deeper breaths
  • In normal therapeutic doses for ADHD , this effect is not noticeable but in higher doses it become obvious

11. Urinary side effects

  • Activation of the alpha adrenergic receptors in the urinary bladder lead to contraction of the bladder sphincter leading to difficulty urinating

12. Mood Swings

  • Higher levels of norepinephrine in certain brain regions lead to mood swings

13. Tics and uncontrolled movements

  • Higher dopamine levels can affect the motor pathways in the brain
  • This may lead to development or exacerbation of motor tics

14. Psychosis

  • Delusions and hallucinations
  • High levels of dopamine can lead to psychotic symptoms, this occur especially with higher doses of the medications

15. Seizures

  • Adderall lowers the seizure threshold by altering the neurotransmitter levels and increases the neuronal excitability
  • This will increase the risk of seizures especially in susceptible people

16. Cognitive effects

  • Long term overstimulation of the brain neurotransmitter systems may lead to cognitive deficits

17. Dependency

  • Higher levels of dopamine in the brain produce a euphoric effect
  • Euphoric effect lead to psychological dependence and potential abuse
  • Euphoric effect require larger doses to be achieved

18. Tolerance and withdrawal

  • Tolerance means with chronic use, higher doses of the medication are needed to achieve the same effect
  • Withdrawal means sudden withdrawal of the medication lead to withdrawal symptoms like fatigue, depression, sleep disturbances …
